summary: Explains how the Lyra sample uses the Gameplay Ability System: ASC on the PlayerState, ability sets, activation groups/policies, game phase abilities, tag relationship mappings, additional costs, health/combat attribute sets and damage/heal executions, with breakdowns of GA_Weapon_Fire, GA_Hero_Dash, GA_Grenade etc.
gotchas: Ability sets granted via Pawn Data/Equipment go to the PlayerState and are not activated until a Pawn is possessed, even with On Spawn policy
On Ability Added fires before Avatar/Input Component may be valid; use On Pawn Avatar Set
Use While Input Active with caution if Retrigger Instanced Ability is set (activation spam)
Health attribute is hidden from modifiers; change it via Healing/Damage executions

summary: Hub page for gameplay programming: links to Gameplay Framework, AI, Physics, Large World Coordinates, data-driven gameplay, Gameplay Ability System, Gameplay Camera System, Targeting System, Input, Vehicles, Networking, Mover and gameplay tutorials.

Describes Blendables (objects implementing IBlendableInterface, mainly post process materials) and the weighted Blendables array in PostProcessSettings on volumes, cameras and scene captures, plus adding them at runtime from Blueprint.
gotchas: AddOrUpdateBlendable never removes entries; set weight to 0 instead
Override checkbox must be set manually or the property is not picked up
Context-sensitive search does not find AddOrUpdateBlendable; disable context sensitive
Array order is opposite to layer stacking; volumes combine by weight and priority

summary: C++ how-to that places a fixed CameraActor and a box trigger actor (BlendTriggerVolume) which switches the player's view to that camera with a blend on overlap and back on exit.
gotchas: Uncheck Constrain Aspect Ratio on the Camera Actor to avoid widescreen letterboxing

summary: Overview of the Replay system: DemoNetDriver and its streamers (Local File, SaveGame, Null, Memory, HTTP), replay data format, checkpoint CVars, and how the Memory Streamer uses static/dynamic level collections for instant replays.
gotchas: Replay actors still call functions that can affect live GameInstance/GameState/GameMode; guard by checking live vs replay level
Null Streamer is deprecated; Local File Streamer cannot read Null Streamer replays
Amortized checkpoint recording can cause slight visual errors on playback
HTTP ServerURL must end with a trailing slash

summary: Hub page for the Chaos Modular Vehicle system; contains only a pointer to its subpages.

How to add voice chat with the EOS Voice Chat plugin via the Lobbies or Trusted Server integration methods using IVoiceChat/IVoiceChatUser, plus eosvoicechat console commands and log categories.
gotchas: Requires configuring the application on the EOS Developer Portal
Trusted Server method needs credentials (client base URL and participant token) from a trusted server
Engine.ini [EOSVoiceChat] section with ProductId/SandboxId/DeploymentId/ClientId/ClientSecret needed when not reusing a Lobbies user

summary: First module of a beginner 3D platformer tutorial series: download the project files and import the UI image files for later modules. Text content is minimal.

Beginner tutorial module outlining Blueprint kill volumes that teleport the player back to the start or last checkpoint, and level checkpoints; page is a short overview.

Beginner platformer module outlining Blueprint obstacles: a moving platform, exploding mines with Niagara and knockback, and a rotating obstacle that sends the player back to a checkpoint; page is a short overview.
Beginner tutorial module about dressing the level with asset packs from the Fab marketplace plus a level design challenge; page is a short overview.
C++ guide to the SaveGame system: subclass USaveGame, then save/load with UGameplayStatics sync, async and binary (memory) functions using slot names and user indices.
gotchas: AsyncSaveGameToSlot is recommended to avoid frame hitches
Binary save/load functions are synchronous only
On development platforms saves are .sav files in Saved/SaveGames

summary: Steps to create a Game Mode Base Blueprint, set its default pawn/HUD/controller classes, assign it as the project default in Maps & Modes, and override it per level in World Settings.
gotchas: Character, HUD, PlayerController, Spectator and Game State classes must be created separately before assigning them in the Game Mode

summary: C++ tutorial in the First Person template: a Cube actor binds OnComponentHit, applies damage when hit by the projectile, swaps to a damaged material on a timer, and the projectile adds an impulse at the hit location.
Hub page for tutorials that recreate common gameplay features; contains no content beyond the intro.

Reference for built-in Blueprint event nodes and their output pins: Level Reset, Actor Begin/End Overlap, Hit, Any/Point/Radial Damage, cursor over, Begin Play, End Play, Destroyed, Tick, Receive Draw HUD, Custom Event.
gotchas: Overlap events need both actors to have Generate Overlap Events and overlap-allowing collision responses
Damage events execute only on the server (local client counts as server in single player)
Event Level Reset only exists in the Level Blueprint; Receive Draw HUD only in HUD subclasses
Event Destroyed will be deprecated; use End Play

summary: Licensee-only instructions for connecting P4V to Epic's licensee Perforce server, creating a workspace on //UE5/Release-Latest and syncing engine source, plus migrating workspaces with p4 flush.

Needs Perforce client 2017.2 or later with SSL
Unused workspaces are aged out after six months

summary: Licensee guide to installing P4V, the single-user connectivity policy, Unicode encoding caveats, and importing Epic engine snapshots into your own local Perforce server.
gotchas: Requires a custom license support agreement with Epic
Only one authorized user may log into the Epic Perforce account
Perforce can corrupt Unicode files stored as text by inserting line-end bytes

summary: Licensee overview of getting Okta/MFA access to Epic's Perforce depot and choosing between Main, Development, Release and Release Stabilization streams.
gotchas: Requires a custom license support agreement with Epic
Only one user per Perforce account
Syncing Release Stabilization streams is not recommended

Running the install script without a USB-connected device does nothing

summary: Explains the Android Single Instance Service (ASIS) plugin, which runs the engine as a long-lived Android service rendering into surfaces owned by separate native client apps (automotive HMI use), its concepts and plugin settings.
gotchas: Requires a source build of UE 5.8 or later
Plugin lives only in source builds under Engine/Restricted/LimitedAccess/Plugins/HMI
Runs as a mediaPlayback foreground service

summary: Lists UAndroidSingleInstanceServiceBPLibrary functions for ASIS: sending/receiving Android events, typed data receiver delegates, and registering cameras, player controllers or game instances as extra-view sources.
FAQ comparing standard GameActivity Android packaging with ASIS single-app and multi-app setups for automotive HMI, covering resource, launch-time and workflow trade-offs.
gotchas: Multi-window support is not yet complete and touch input will not work
ASIS does not reduce resource usage for a single app built fully in Unreal
App is split across two APKs

summary: Short guide to switching the ASIS example client to multiview by changing its AndroidManifest.xml activity to ActivityForMultiview; the template already registers two extra cameras in the Level Blueprint.

gotchas: AARs require Enable asis libs generation; example client requires Compile ASISProject

summary: Set up ASIS either from the TP_HMI_ASIS template or by adding it to an existing project: enable plugins, add staging remap directories, set AsisGameEngine, and enable plugin settings.
gotchas: Cannot be used with a launcher (binary) engine install; needs UE 5.8+ source build
Restricted plugins are stripped at staging unless remapped
Custom GameEngine classes must derive from UAsisGameEngine to keep render intervals

summary: Java reference for the ASIS client app: linking the AARs, building an ASISConnection, wrapping surfaces in ASISMainViewClient/ASISExtraViewClient, sending data/console commands/touch, the attach sequence and per-view render intervals.
gotchas: Extra-view client IDs must match the IDs used in RegisterCameraForAsis etc.
Render interval applies only to extra views; main view renders every tick

summary: Shows how to use Preview Equivalent C++ Header to view a Blueprint class or struct as C++ declarations (variables, functions, components, event dispatchers), with sort and style options.
How to visually diff Blueprints and Blueprint-adjacent assets, against each other or source control revisions, plus the Perforce-only UE Review Tool for changelists.
gotchas: Only Blueprints and Blueprint-adjacent asset types are supported
UE Review Tool supports Perforce only

summary: Step-by-step process to record graphics PSOs with -logPSO, expand them with the ShaderPipelineCacheTools commandlet into a .spc stable cache, bundle it in Build/<Platform>/PipelineCaches, verify coverage, and control compilation/usage masks and user cache.
gotchas: Runtime PSO precaching is usually enough; this is for extra coverage
Caches are per RHI (D3D12 cache unusable on Vulkan); D3D11 and ray tracing PSOs not supported
Project name and shader format in the .spc filename must match exactly
Stale caches lengthen load times; recollect after major content changes
